config.jbMerge.autoOpen.markdownDescript: Open conflicted files in Merge Studio and show the conflicts dashboard when a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, git am or stash pop stops on conflicts. If a GitStudio with the same Conflicts dashboard is installed with `#gitstudio.merge.autoOpen#` on, GitStudio does this instead.
config.undefined.title: Merge Studio
description: Resolve Git merge and rebase conflicts in a JetBrains-style three-pane editor, with a conflicts dashboard, colour-coded changes, full undo and a side-by-side diff.
displayName: Merge Studio — Merge Conflict Resolver & 3-Way Merge Editor
walkthrough.mergeStudio.gettingStarted.d: Resolve merge and rebase conflicts in three panes: yours, result, theirs.
walkthrough.mergeStudio.gettingStarted.m: At the first conflict Merge Studio asks whether to turn off VS Code's own merge editor and conflict highlights: Turn them off, Not now, or Don't ask again.

At your first conflict, Merge Studio asks whether to turn off VS Code's own merge editor and conflict highlights, so they don't open alongside it. Changed your mind later? Put them back with one command.
[Restore VS Code's merge editor](command:jbMerge.restoreBuiltInMergeEditor)
Choose your merge editor

The legend names the four colours and how many of each are left: Conflict, 3; Same on both sides, 2; One side only, 2; Removed lines, 1. Below it the sample merge wears them: conflicts in orange, the same change on both sides in green, changes made on one side only in blue, a removed line in grey, and one change already taken from Theirs kept as a faint blue trace.

Each colour says whether your choice matters. Orange: a conflict, you choose (Resolve simple on the toolbar settles the ones whose edits don't overlap). Green: the same change on both sides, so either arrow takes it. Blue: a change on one side only, safe to take. Grey: lines removed without a conflict. The legend names them in words, and a change you settled keeps a lighter trace of the side you took.
Read the colours
The foot of the Conflicts dashboard mid-rebase: conflicted files with Accept Yours, Accept Theirs and Merge…, then Abort Rebase, and Continue Rebase waiting until no file has conflicts.

When the last file is resolved, press Continue. Abort takes you back to where you started, and Skip appears where git offers it (a cherry-pick, a revert, a patch).
[Show my conflicts](command:jbMerge.showConflicts)
Finish the whole operation from the dashboard
Mid-rebase: YOURS test, onto, THEIRS master. The left pane is your commit being replayed from test; the right pane is master with the commits already rebased onto it.
In a rebase, git calls your own commit “theirs”. Merge Studio doesn't: Yours is always your work, on the left, with both branch names on screen.
Rebase without swapping sides
Two files selected in the Explorer and the context menu's Compare in Merge Studio, over the side-by-side diff it opened.

Select two files in the Explorer, right-click, and choose Compare in Merge Studio. Or start with a sample.
[Open sample diff](command:jbMerge.openDemoDiff)
Merge Studio is free and open source. [Support Merge Studio…](command:jbMerge.support)
Compare two files
The sample merge, nothing resolved yet: YOURS feature/session-hardening on the left, the result in the middle, THEIRS main on the right, the toolbar above and Apply below.

A ready-made rebase stop, no setup needed, with every kind of change in it. Take a change with the arrows beside it, or edit the result yourself, then press Apply to see what a real Apply does.
[Open sample merge](command:jbMerge.openDemo)
Resolve a sample conflict
Settings with both installed: GitStudio's Merge: Auto Open is on, so GitStudio opens conflicts and Merge Studio stays quiet; turning it off lets Merge Studio open them.

GitStudio ships this same merge editor and conflicts dashboard. With both installed, GitStudio opens conflicts automatically and Merge Studio stays quiet. Its commands (Resolve Conflicts…, Open Sample Merge, Compare) still work and open the same screens.
[Let Merge Studio open conflicts instead](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22gitstudio.merge.autoOpen%22%5D)
